summary: Thoroughly preregistered, well-instrumented confirmatory run that produced an artifact-backed null (ceiling) result: both baseline and guarded conditions succeeded on all 200 held-out tasks, making the preregistered AUC-based primary estimand uncomputable. Execution and many low-level artifacts (per-episode responses, validator traces, manifests, hashes) are present and well-documented; one notable artifact omission (serialized trained-composite-model weights) is candidly disclosed. The manuscript is honest about limitations and yields useful methodological lessons, but requires targeted clarifications and additional artifact-referencing to meet reproducibility and claim-precision norms.
critical_issues: Primary preregistered estimand (AUC-ROC difference composite vs best submetric) is uncomputable on the held-out test because there are zero positive outage labels in both conditions; this eliminates the confirmatory discriminative comparison central to the study’s original claim.

A serialized trained-composite-model (weights) artifact was not persisted into the evidence bundle (execution omission). The manuscript must either attach the persisted training artifact (if present) or explicitly document the absence and point readers to the exact artifacts that justify the reported composite-score behavior.

The manuscript currently does not present descriptive summaries of per-task submetrics and (if available) composite scores on the held-out test (means, variances, ranges). Without these summaries, readers cannot verify the claim that the test set exhibited a ceiling effect or inspect whether submetric variation could have enabled discriminative evaluation.

Key reproducibility trace: the paper asserts composite scores were computed and applied, but does not cite the exact file path(s) and SHA-256(s) for (a) the computed composite scores on test, and (b) training diagnostics (cross-validation folds, selected hyperparameters). This gap impedes independent verification from the supplied bundle.
required_revisions: Add a concise table/paragraph in Results that reports descriptive statistics (N, mean, SD, min, max, and count of distinct values) for each pre-registered submetric on the held-out test set: verifier-coverage fraction, canary-sim pass rate, rollback-success probability, LLM confidence, and abstention-utility. Source these numbers to explicit artifact paths (execution/scoring/*.json or a summarized CSV) and include the artifact SHA-256(s). This must be drawn solely from the supplied scoring JSONs / analysis CSVs.

Either (A) include the serialized trained-composite-model artifact (weights file) into the evidence bundle and reference its file path and SHA-256 in the manuscript, or (B) if the weights file truly does not exist, add an explicit, prominent statement in Methods/Disclosure that the serialized weights are absent, explain exactly which persisted artifacts were used instead to compute composite scores on test (e.g., precomputed composite-score CSV with path and SHA-256), and discuss implications for reproducibility. Do not claim the weights are available if they are not.

Cite the exact artifact(s) that contain the computed composite scores applied to test (file path(s) and SHA-256). If a precomputed composite-score file is present in the bundle, include a brief table of composite-score distribution (mean, SD, percentiles) for the test split; if not present, state explicitly that composite scores are unavailable and explain how the conclusion (AUC uncomputable) was drawn from the existing artifacts (refer to paired_contingency_table.csv and condition_summary.csv with SHA-256s already present).

Tighten the paper’s framing of the contribution in the Introduction and Conclusion to emphasize that the result is an artifact-backed methodological null (ceiling effect) specific to the supplied synthetic task bank, emulator determinism, and gpt-5-mini; remove or further qualify any wording that could be read as claiming broader empirical evidence about composite-score ineffectiveness beyond these artifacts.
optional_revisions: Provide a short appendix or inline table giving representative per-task submetric vectors (e.g., 10 test-task rows) with paths and SHA-256s to the corresponding execution/scoring JSONs to aid reviewer inspection.

Discuss more explicitly the choice to use a shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation=false) and its implications for external validity; reference the provider_call audit entries showing model_calls_used=200 and explain why shared-generation was appropriate for the intended guarded vs baseline comparison.

If available in the bundle, add cross-validation diagnostics (train+val CV mean AUC/AUPRC, chosen regularization parameter) as an artifact reference; if not available, state this omission and suggest the minimal artifact set needed for full reproducibility in a follow-up.

Briefly discuss alternative estimands or small post-hoc descriptive discriminative checks (e.g., rank-order overlap between composite scores and single submetrics) performed on the test set and cite artifact outputs; label these clearly as exploratory.
